name: Engine oil filter console with integrated galleries, AlSi10Mg concept F0
description: Independent concept of a 993 console combining filter seat, two non-collinear galleries and two ports in a single body. The sources establish the part numbers, a commercial mass and the MAHLE OC 229 filter interface, but no OEM geometry; all F0 interfaces remain synthetic.

classification.intended_use: F0 screening of open CAD, DfAM value, hot/cold pressure loss, pressure, threads, thermal, mass and cleanliness; no manufacture, sealing, installation, oil circulation or start-up authorized

provenance.record_license: MIT for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, Porsche/PorscheFanatics/OEMVWShop/MAHLE/Islandworks/EOS surface or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - 993 engine oil filter console and filter
sources.notes: Identifies consoles 993 107 057 00/01 and the engine filters including 993 107 203 03/MAHLE OC 229; no geometry and no material. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-OIL-FILTER-CONSOLE-CANDIDATE.

sources.title: OEMVWShop - Porsche console 993 107 057 01
sources.notes: Declares 0.78 kg with no weighing boundary and no protocol; mass comparison only. See SRC-OEMVWSHOP-993-OIL-FILTER-CONSOLE-MASS.

sources.title: MHTeile - MAHLE OC 229 filter for Porsche 993
sources.notes: Publishes a 76 x 101 mm filter, M20x1.5; distributor data add 72/62 mm, 20 Nm and 333 g. These dimensions concern the filter, not the console. See SRC-MAHLERETAIL-OC229-993-FILTER-INTERFACE.

sources.title: Islandworks - integrated thermostat/filter console, 6061-T6
sources.notes: Functional precedent in 6061-T6 billet using a 993 filter; it is not a 993 replacement part and no geometry is reused. See SRC-ISLANDWORKS-INTEGRATED-THERMOSTAT-FILTER-CONSOLE-6061.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - 993 manual data
sources.notes: Unverified OCR occurrence: about 6.5 bar at 5,000 rpm and 90 °C for the Carrera. Used as a regression reference, never as a released load case. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-MANUAL-DATA.

sources.title: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg material data sheet
sources.notes: T6 route and candidate material; numerical values of the calculation kept as generic comparisons. See SRC-EOS-ALSI10MG-CURRENT-PAGE.

material.grade: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg T6 for comparison; analogous commercial architecture in 6061-T6 billet
material.standard: DIN EN 1706 EN AC-43000 and ASTM F3318 for the candidate; program-specific oil, sealing and cleanliness specification to be contracted

post_processing: orientation and supports ensuring all galleries are open, to be qualified
stress relief then T6 with distortion and porosity monitored
HIP to be decided on fatigue, sealing and tomography results
machining of the case face, ports, drillings, bosses, filter seat and M20x1.5 thread
validated internal deburring, powder removal, flushing and particle extraction
surface treatment compatible with oil, seals, threads and temperature
final packaging to engine cleanliness standards
supplier_requirements: traceable machine, parameters, orientation, supports, powder and batch
oriented coupons with tensile, fatigue, oil corrosion and hot pressure tests
gallery witnesses for roughness, powder removal and residual cleanliness
full CT, FPI and metallography with zoned defect criteria
metrology of the datums, ports, case face, thread, filter seat and drillings
proof of pressure, burst, leakage, flow, thermal cycling, vibration and engine endurance

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Qualify AlSi10Mg against case, studs, inserts, sensors, fittings, filter and oil; address corrosion, fretting and differential expansion.

known_limits: PorscheFanatics identifies the part and the filter but provides neither geometry nor material.
The 0.78 kg mass is a commercial claim with no protocol and no weighing boundary.
The 76 x 101 mm, M20x1.5 and 72/62 mm dimensions concern the OC 229 filter, not the console.
The 144 x 90 x 50 mm body, the four mounting points, two ports and two galleries are entirely synthetic.
The 6.5 bar pressure is an unverified OCR occurrence; flow, viscosities, local losses and roughness are scenarios.
The filter, its bypass valve and the engine circuit are absent from the hydraulic calculation.
The cold screen and the constrained thermal screen fail.
No internal cleanliness, sealing, fatigue, corrosion, CHT-CFD or engine integration is demonstrated.
The STEP proves only a re-readable BREP; no manufacture, oil circulation or start-up is authorized.
